00:07:58,441 --> 00:08:00,842
A plain push does not send tags.

128
00:08:01,178 --> 00:08:03,655
The tag holds only your own work.

129
00:08:03,655 --> 00:08:07,783
No participant material, including de-identified notes.

130
00:08:07,783 --> 00:08:11,987
No credentials, session logs or unrelated personal data.

131
00:08:12,328 --> 00:08:17,193
The teaching team runs one model review on your tag and sends you a copy;

132
00:08:17,193 --> 00:08:18,392
keep it unchanged.

133
00:08:18,392 --> 00:08:21,124
Check out the tag in a separate worktree,

134
00:08:21,124 --> 00:08:24,190
and verify every finding through the launcher.

135
00:08:24,190 --> 00:08:25,656
Plan about five hours.

136
00:08:26,694 --> 00:08:29,263
M3 is worth three points, one each.

137
00:08:29,263 --> 00:08:31,244
Evidence that can be rerun.

138
00:08:31,244 --> 00:08:34,106
Evidence that supports each conclusion,

139
00:08:34,106 --> 00:08:38,288
telling a demonstrated result from an untested suspicion.

140
00:08:38,288 --> 00:08:41,590
And one check of your own, with its boundary.

141
00:08:41,928 --> 00:08:46,540
The number or severity of the model's findings does not set the score.

142
00:08:46,540 --> 00:08:47,791
Your evidence does.

143
00:08:47,791 --> 00:08:50,229
And confirmed findings carry into M4.

144
00:08:50,578 --> 00:08:54,583
When evidence conflicts, it goes to the human integrity process.

145
00:08:54,583 --> 00:08:58,589
An automatic authorship detector does not decide responsibility.

146
00:08:59,628 --> 00:09:04,329
So mark each claim confirmed, refuted or cannot tell, as in Week 6.

147
00:09:04,329 --> 00:09:07,557
The record writes cannot tell as undetermined.

148
00:09:07,894 --> 00:09:10,913
Each one is judged against the frozen requirements,

149
00:09:10,913 --> 00:09:15,116
and decided by what a check observed, not by the wording of the review.

150
00:09:15,461 --> 00:09:16,667
One question to try.

151
00:09:16,667 --> 00:09:19,801
On your own tag, which path did the audit not cover,

152
00:09:19,801 --> 00:09:21,731
and what command would check it?

episodes.title: Keep the layers apart
episodes.decision: keep the layers apart, and check each one on its own. A finding has three layers, observation, hypothesis and change, written in separate fields. A generated change is a claim until one task check runs on the page: proposal A looks right (labelled, reached by keyboard, query check green) and does not help, because its selection never reaches the query. Each check answers only its own question (the query check, the request line, the keyboard walk, a new authorized session), and the iteration is accepted only for the checked scope. M4 turns each Week 12 result into the response that result selects, and a repair starts with a test that fails on the frozen snapshot. Across an organization the same separation holds: the portal's grants, the gateway's key and budgets, the cost of an accepted change and the evaluator that routing depends on are separate layers, each checked on replayed records, generation first, then verification. The demo shows the same moves in eight minutes.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,582
Here is a course-authored interface.

2
00:00:02,582 --> 00:00:06,526
Its visible controls are Overview, Options and Refresh.

3
00:00:06,526 --> 00:00:10,972
Inside Options, a State filter offers All, Failed and Running.

4
00:00:10,972 --> 00:00:15,418
The task: find the most recent failed build in pipeline Alpha.

5
00:00:15,767 --> 00:00:19,908
The supplied record says the user opens Overview, then returns.

6
00:00:19,908 --> 00:00:24,181
They select Refresh twice, and ask where failed builds are shown.

7
00:00:24,181 --> 00:00:25,891
The task is not completed.

8
00:00:26,233 --> 00:00:29,302
Yet the query returns the correct failed records.

9
00:00:29,302 --> 00:00:33,873
So behavior correctness and locating the control are different questions.

10
00:00:34,217 --> 00:00:36,917
Before going on, write an observation,

11
00:00:36,917 --> 00:00:40,328
a hypothesis and a candidate change of your own.

12
00:00:40,328 --> 00:00:45,943
The record contains no real participant, timestamp or population-level finding.

13
00:00:48,483 --> 00:00:51,212
The observation is what the record shows.

14
00:00:51,212 --> 00:00:56,668
"Options may not communicate status filtering" is an interpretation: a hypothesis.

15
00:00:57,017 --> 00:01:01,621
Write them in separate fields, before asking an assistant for a patch.

16
00:01:01,621 --> 00:01:05,632
If they share one sentence, split them before implementation.

17
00:01:05,632 --> 00:01:09,579
And this is a reasoning aid, not a claim about a population.

18
00:01:10,616 --> 00:01:15,801
Exposing Status: All is one plausible change to test, not a proven solution.

19
00:01:15,801 --> 00:01:20,167
The bounded request: add the control to the existing build page,

20
00:01:20,167 --> 00:01:23,306
and preserve the query contract, result order,

21
00:01:23,306 --> 00:01:26,034
permission check and keyboard operation.

22
00:01:26,383 --> 00:01:31,482
Two recorded replies answer it, a course-authored replay; no model wrote them.

23
00:01:31,482 --> 00:01:32,790
Both say a labelled,

24
00:01:32,790 --> 00:01:37,366
keyboard-operable Status control now puts failed builds one step away.

25
00:01:37,700 --> 00:01:41,979
Proposal A adds a new select and leaves Options unchanged.

26
00:01:41,979 --> 00:01:45,815
Proposal B moves the existing select out of Options.

27
00:01:45,815 --> 00:01:49,136
Predict: will the task complete on each page?

28
00:01:52,682 --> 00:01:54,840
Verification is one task check.

29
00:01:54,840 --> 00:01:59,434
It tries the task the way a keyboard user would: Tab from the top,

30
00:01:59,434 --> 00:02:04,864
open a menu or choose an option only on a word from the task, follow no links,

31
00:02:04,864 --> 00:02:07,857
then press the first submit button reached.

32
00:02:08,199 --> 00:02:12,300
The task is completed when the first row shown is build 121,

33
00:02:12,300 --> 00:02:15,650
and every control reached has an accessible name.

34
00:02:15,650 --> 00:02:19,136
The check reads the page as text and never runs it.

35
00:02:20,182 --> 00:02:24,738
Our run of proposal A, in a scratch copy, prints what the notes print.

36
00:02:24,738 --> 00:02:30,074
The query check passes, and the walk reaches the Status select and chooses Failed.

37
00:02:30,416 --> 00:02:36,317
But the request sends state equals failed, and the dashboard reads status,

38
00:02:36,317 --> 00:02:41,181
which the old State select inside Options still sends as all.

39
00:02:41,181 --> 00:02:45,089
So the rows shown are 123 running and 122 passed.

40
00:02:45,089 --> 00:02:46,205
Not completed.

41
00:02:46,549 --> 00:02:50,506
That runnable observation refutes the reply's claim.

42
00:02:50,506 --> 00:02:56,442
Proposal B sends status failed, shows build 121 first, and completes the task.

43
00:02:56,442 --> 00:03:00,400
Exit zero; the current page and proposal A exit one.

44
00:03:01,448 --> 00:03:04,381
Each check answers a different question.

45
00:03:04,381 --> 00:03:08,268
The query check: the query still returns 121 and 119.

46
00:03:08,268 --> 00:03:11,714
The request line: what the page actually sends.

47
00:03:11,714 --> 00:03:16,774
The keyboard walk: a named control is reached without opening a menu.

48
00:03:17,115 --> 00:03:21,205
None of them shows that a person finds the control without a hint;

49
00:03:21,205 --> 00:03:24,861
only a new authorized session on the accepted revision can.

50
00:03:24,861 --> 00:03:26,968
The check matches words literally.

51
00:03:26,968 --> 00:03:31,244
And the old session cannot show that the new label is understandable.

52
00:03:32,281 --> 00:03:35,981
If proposal B passes the task, query and keyboard checks,

53
00:03:35,981 --> 00:03:40,850
and an authorized new session completes the task without a navigation hint,

54
00:03:40,850 --> 00:03:43,706
accept the iteration for that checked scope.

55
00:03:44,048 --> 00:03:47,284
Record the revision, the inputs and the results.

56
00:03:47,284 --> 00:03:50,317
Do not claim that all users will now succeed.

57
00:03:51,364 --> 00:03:54,645
M4 turns each Week 12 result into a response.

58
00:03:54,645 --> 00:03:59,237
Where a finding came from is no reason to accept or dismiss it;

59
00:03:59,237 --> 00:04:00,768
the evidence decides.

60
00:04:01,114 --> 00:04:03,991
Confirmed: repair, or defer with an owner.

61
00:04:03,991 --> 00:04:08,100
Refuted: no change, keeping the refuting command and output.

62
00:04:08,100 --> 00:04:13,306
Cannot tell: investigate, naming the missing observation and the next check.

63
00:04:13,306 --> 00:04:18,854
A scope check with no defect observed: no change, keeping its range and boundary.

64
00:04:19,197 --> 00:04:23,319
Never turn cannot tell into no change because nothing has failed yet.

65
00:04:24,364 --> 00:04:27,496
A repair is written from the frozen requirement.

66
00:04:27,496 --> 00:04:32,389
For a record you confirmed against R1, no role reads a private report body,

67
00:04:32,389 --> 00:04:34,999
test the case before you touch the code.

68
00:04:35,347 --> 00:04:38,625
Run it through the launcher on the frozen snapshot:

69
00:04:38,625 --> 00:04:43,380
a confirmed defect makes it fail, and that output is your evidence before.

70
00:04:43,380 --> 00:04:45,436
If it passes, settle that first.

71
00:04:45,781 --> 00:04:51,195
Then fix from R1, run the same test again, keep both outputs with their revisions,

72
00:04:51,195 --> 00:04:53,770
and rerun the rule's other three cases,

73
00:04:53,770 --> 00:04:58,656
so the fix neither blocks a permitted reader nor lets anyone else through.

74
00:04:59,697 --> 00:05:05,275
Week 11's launcher broker keeps the key outside the work, fixes the destination,

75
00:05:05,275 --> 00:05:08,133
caps each run and keeps a minimal record.

76
00:05:08,133 --> 00:05:13,571
When a whole organization adopts agents, those jobs move into shared services.

77
00:05:13,914 --> 00:05:19,260
Four pieces recur: a tool portal, a model gateway, cost per accepted change,

78
00:05:19,260 --> 00:05:20,105
and routing.

79
00:05:20,105 --> 00:05:25,733
Each concentrates authority, so each needs a check that would reveal it failing.

80
00:05:26,080 --> 00:05:30,936
So keep these layers apart too: the grants, the key and budgets, the cost,

81
00:05:30,936 --> 00:05:34,741
and the evaluator behind routing, each checked on its own.

82
00:05:35,080 --> 00:05:39,344
Each part of the practice is a replayed record with an agent's summary,

83
00:05:39,344 --> 00:05:40,364
which is a claim.

84
00:05:40,364 --> 00:05:44,868
Check by hand, write the result you expect, then run the check and compare.

85
00:05:45,913 --> 00:05:51,704
A tool portal lists which tools exist, who may call each, and records every grant.

86
00:05:51,704 --> 00:05:56,153
One revocation reaches every agent; so does one mistaken grant.

87
00:05:56,497 --> 00:06:00,029
Checking each call against its grant is not enough:

88
00:06:00,029 --> 00:06:04,531
if the grant reaches more than the task needs, every call passes.

89
00:06:04,880 --> 00:06:08,089
In our own record, the task needs only guide-site,

90
00:06:08,089 --> 00:06:10,913
and the summary says every call was allowed.

91
00:06:10,913 --> 00:06:13,737
We ran the course's check in a scratch copy;

92
00:06:13,737 --> 00:06:16,304
the course runs it through the launcher.

93
00:06:16,647 --> 00:06:20,991
The summary is true, but grant P2 reaches every repository,

94
00:06:20,991 --> 00:06:25,409
so call two read a private log outside the task: over-broad.

95
00:06:25,409 --> 00:06:30,196
Narrowed in a copy, call two is denied, and the tool did not run.

96
00:06:30,530 --> 00:06:36,277
Give each grant an owner, a reason, and a test that a call outside it is denied.

97
00:06:37,313 --> 00:06:42,064
A shared gateway holds keys, budgets, rate limits and request logs.

98
00:06:42,064 --> 00:06:46,389
Replay its policy over its own records: a request over a cap,

99
00:06:46,389 --> 00:06:51,140
or on an unlisted route, should show as refused before it was sent.

100
00:06:51,479 --> 00:06:54,813
Our record claims every run followed the policy:

101
00:06:54,813 --> 00:06:58,077
three requests and two thousand tokens per run.

102
00:06:58,077 --> 00:07:01,063
Each request reserves its worst case first,

103
00:07:01,063 --> 00:07:06,688
yet run two's third was sent with fifteen hundred used and nine hundred reserved.

104
00:07:07,029 --> 00:07:09,706
And a sandbox-side log line holds the key.

105
00:07:09,706 --> 00:07:13,084
Even a placeholder key belongs only with the gateway,

106
00:07:13,084 --> 00:07:16,016
which in this course is the launcher's broker.

107
00:07:17,062 --> 00:07:22,827
A trace total measures one run, but an accepted change costs every run behind it,

108
00:07:22,827 --> 00:07:28,522
failed and retried ones included, plus runs on rejected changes and review time.

109
00:07:28,522 --> 00:07:32,294
Cost per token rewards cheap output nobody can merge.

110
00:07:32,628 --> 00:07:37,758
Our record: fourteen units and fifty review minutes over two accepted changes,

111
00:07:37,758 --> 00:07:42,625
so seven units and twenty-five minutes each, not the trace total of three.

112
00:07:42,625 --> 00:07:44,598
Units are made up, not prices.

113
00:07:44,945 --> 00:07:49,918
Routing sends each task to the cheapest route that passes the evaluator.

114
00:07:49,918 --> 00:07:54,270
A cheaper route is good enough only if it loses no frozen case:

115
00:07:54,270 --> 00:07:57,792
every case the current route passes, it passes too.

116
00:07:57,792 --> 00:08:01,798
Ours passes nine of ten and loses case six: not supported,

117
00:08:01,798 --> 00:08:04,009
though it clears ninety percent.

118
00:08:04,345 --> 00:08:07,675
Rerun those cases whenever a route or model changes;

119
00:08:07,675 --> 00:08:10,812
even a full pass says nothing about other inputs.

120
00:08:11,861 --> 00:08:15,334
The expo demonstration is a communication exercise,

121
00:08:15,334 --> 00:08:19,489
not a second test or a substitute for the individual defense.

122
00:08:19,827 --> 00:08:22,161
Give each move a visible artifact.

123
00:08:22,161 --> 00:08:26,829
Need and finding, a minute each, with the hypothesis labelled apart.

124
00:08:26,829 --> 00:08:30,056
Change, two minutes, and what stayed unchanged.

125
00:08:30,394 --> 00:08:34,242
Verification, two minutes, expected result first.

126
00:08:34,242 --> 00:08:39,111
Decision, one minute: repair, defer, no change or investigate.

127
00:08:39,111 --> 00:08:45,394
Limit, one minute: what this evidence supports, and what still needs a new test.

128
00:08:45,744 --> 00:08:49,326
Do not paste participant identities, raw recordings,

129
00:08:49,326 --> 00:08:52,977
private code or model transcripts into what you show.

130
00:08:54,011 --> 00:08:59,805
So keep the layers apart, and let each check answer its own question: for a finding,

131
00:08:59,805 --> 00:09:02,289
for a page, and for an organization.

132
00:09:02,627 --> 00:09:07,451
C2 is due at the end of this week, or the day before your defense,

133
00:09:07,451 --> 00:09:09,059
whichever comes first.

134
00:09:09,394 --> 00:09:10,602
One question to try.

135
00:09:10,602 --> 00:09:13,502
What would you check if the label changed again?

136
00:09:13,502 --> 00:09:17,971
Name the new input, the expected effect, and the decision that would move.

137
00:09:17,971 --> 00:09:22,804
If the existing test cannot see the changed condition, name the different check.

episodes.title: Has it ever failed?
episodes.decision: claim only the scope you checked, and count a check as evidence that it would stop a bad change only once you have seen it fail. In the practice packet the code predicts that a guest is denied, but the evidence matrix never observed a guest, so acceptance extends only to the checked cases; a peer's changed input either reuses an observation or names the next check. The same rule decides the software-factory claim stage by stage. The Evaluate stage's regression gate has been seen to fail on an agent's "robust" evaluator change and to pass on the current evaluator, so it is a candidate for unattended merging, not yet unattended: its cases sit where the agent could write, the candidate runs inside the checker, and the stop rule has never been exercised. Its nine cases also pass a trim-only escape until that escape becomes a tenth case. The model audit has never been seen to fail and pass on known inputs, so it runs unattended only as a source of hypotheses.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,858
The agreed policy permits an edit exactly when owner or staff is true,

2
00:00:04,858 --> 00:00:06,385
and archived is false.

3
00:00:06,385 --> 00:00:09,369
A guest means both role booleans are false.

4
00:00:09,717 --> 00:00:12,460
This continues the Week 6 dashboard case,

5
00:00:12,460 --> 00:00:15,606
whose earlier guard let an archived owner edit.

6
00:00:15,606 --> 00:00:18,282
The repaired guard groups the two roles.

7
00:00:18,282 --> 00:00:21,629
If allowed, the title becomes the requested title.

8
00:00:21,967 --> 00:00:26,045
The supplied evidence matrix covers active owner and staff,

9
00:00:26,045 --> 00:00:30,332
both allowed with the new title, and archived owner and staff,

10
00:00:30,332 --> 00:00:32,475
both denied with the old title.

11
00:00:32,475 --> 00:00:34,065
Guest cases are absent.

12
00:00:34,065 --> 00:00:38,697
Predict an active guest's decision and final title before going on.

13
00:00:42,233 --> 00:00:46,359
The code predicts denial and an unchanged title for a guest.

14
00:00:46,359 --> 00:00:49,385
But the provided matrix has not observed it.

15
00:00:49,733 --> 00:00:51,187
State that distinction,

16
00:00:51,187 --> 00:00:55,609
and propose the guest request with both response and state assertions.

17
00:00:55,609 --> 00:00:58,895
If those checks then complete on the repaired guard,

18
00:00:58,895 --> 00:01:01,738
acceptance can extend to those checked cases.

19
00:01:02,783 --> 00:01:05,551
Rehearse one claim small enough to defend:

20
00:01:05,551 --> 00:01:08,518
for the tested role and archive combinations,

21
00:01:08,518 --> 00:01:12,407
archived builds remain unchanged when an edit is requested.

22
00:01:12,407 --> 00:01:15,043
It names a behavior and a checked scope.

23
00:01:15,383 --> 00:01:17,434
Behind it sits a causal account.

24
00:01:17,434 --> 00:01:19,613
Archived content needs protection.

25
00:01:19,613 --> 00:01:21,921
The old owner term bypassed archive.

26
00:01:21,921 --> 00:01:24,933
The new grouping applies archive to both roles.

27
00:01:24,933 --> 00:01:29,292
And the archived-owner regression checks denial and unchanged state.

28
00:01:29,633 --> 00:01:34,736
On the repaired guard, that check was observed: deny, and the title stays Old.

29
00:01:34,736 --> 00:01:37,876
So the conclusion covers the checked cases only.

30
00:01:38,216 --> 00:01:41,906
A peer's changed input then takes one of two branches.

31
00:01:41,906 --> 00:01:44,365
Already observed: cite the evidence.

32
00:01:44,365 --> 00:01:48,943
Not observed, like the guest: predict from the code, add the check,

33
00:01:48,943 --> 00:01:50,514
and say it has not run.

34
00:01:50,514 --> 00:01:54,819
A complete spoken explanation does not create missing evidence.

35
00:01:55,866 --> 00:02:00,915
In rehearsal, a peer changes one condition, and you answer independently.

36
00:02:00,915 --> 00:02:06,103
Staff may now edit archived builds; owners who are not staff still may not.

37
00:02:06,103 --> 00:02:09,077
That needs its own authorization and cases,

38
00:02:09,077 --> 00:02:12,189
not a silent rewrite of the old expectations.

39
00:02:12,532 --> 00:02:17,593
Now the evaluation question changes, from "is the status exactly failed",

40
00:02:17,593 --> 00:02:20,505
to "did the build finish without passing".

41
00:02:20,505 --> 00:02:25,982
That needs a new accepted contract and scorer cases: canceled now requires yes,

42
00:02:25,982 --> 00:02:27,784
running still requires no,

43
00:02:27,784 --> 00:02:31,805
and an earlier pass is evidence for the old question only.

44
00:02:32,149 --> 00:02:37,556
A rollback command reports success, and no request has reached the service since.

45
00:02:37,556 --> 00:02:40,961
The message describes the command, not the service:

46
00:02:40,961 --> 00:02:44,633
the previous revision or the faulty one may be serving.

47
00:02:44,633 --> 00:02:49,773
Observe the service itself, then one user request, before declaring recovery.

48
00:02:50,815 --> 00:02:54,080
M4 is worth three of your twenty project points:

49
00:02:54,080 --> 00:02:59,182
respond to the confirmed audit findings, make a justified usability change,

50
00:02:59,182 --> 00:03:01,087
and demonstrate at the expo.

51
00:03:01,087 --> 00:03:05,984
The review response carries one and a half points; the other three rows,

52
00:03:05,984 --> 00:03:07,209
half a point each.

53
00:03:07,549 --> 00:03:10,090
The expo runs in the Week 14 workshop.

54
00:03:10,090 --> 00:03:15,039
Everyone demonstrates at once, staff and classmates move between stations,

55
00:03:15,039 --> 00:03:18,517
and each of you answers at least one staff question.

56
00:03:18,517 --> 00:03:23,733
It does not replace your own defense, in Week 13 or 14, so rehearse before it.

57
00:03:24,082 --> 00:03:26,577
At your station, show one user task,

58
00:03:26,577 --> 00:03:30,182
its visible behavior and the check that supports it.

59
00:03:30,182 --> 00:03:35,727
Identify the actual revision, and explain a decision and the limit that remains.

60
00:03:36,065 --> 00:03:40,328
If the live path fails, keep that result and state the next observation.

61
00:03:40,328 --> 00:03:44,176
Use a labelled recording only if the announced format permits it,

62
00:03:44,176 --> 00:03:46,839
and never relabel an older result as current.

63
00:03:47,881 --> 00:03:51,649
A software factory organizes requirements, generation,

64
00:03:51,649 --> 00:03:55,277
verification and delivery into a repeatable process.

65
00:03:55,277 --> 00:04:00,300
The stronger claim is that its stages could run with little human input.

66
00:04:00,300 --> 00:04:03,090
Treat that as a claim, not a conclusion.

67
00:04:03,431 --> 00:04:06,088
Test it on your own ci-dashboard pipeline.

68
00:04:06,088 --> 00:04:09,377
For each stage, ask whether it could run unattended,

69
00:04:09,377 --> 00:04:11,907
and what evidence would be needed first.

70
00:04:12,948 --> 00:04:18,573
The Evaluate stage already has an executable gate, from the M2 evaluator workshop.

71
00:04:18,573 --> 00:04:22,758
It copies the evaluator and its cases into a fresh workspace,

72
00:04:22,758 --> 00:04:27,217
runs the cases through the launcher, and exits with their status.

73
00:04:27,565 --> 00:04:30,908
Here the evaluator answers the Week 10 contract:

74
00:04:30,908 --> 00:04:33,416
is a supplied status exactly failed?

75
00:04:33,416 --> 00:04:38,919
Only the exact string yes is correct for failed, and only no for anything else.

76
00:04:38,919 --> 00:04:40,800
Nine frozen cases check it.

77
00:04:41,148 --> 00:04:43,859
Generation: an agent proposes a change,

78
00:04:43,859 --> 00:04:46,987
a course-authored replay that no model wrote.

79
00:04:46,987 --> 00:04:50,462
Its reply says: made scoring robust to formatting.

80
00:04:50,462 --> 00:04:52,964
Answers are trimmed and lower-cased,

81
00:04:52,964 --> 00:04:57,135
and an answer that starts with the expected word now counts.

82
00:04:57,481 --> 00:04:59,666
Would an unattended pipeline merge it?

83
00:04:59,666 --> 00:05:02,195
Predict the gate's exit code before the run.

84
00:05:05,731 --> 00:05:11,466
To verify, the course runs the gate on the proposal, then on the current evaluator.

85
00:05:11,466 --> 00:05:15,750
We ran the same cases in a scratch copy, without the launcher.

86
00:05:15,750 --> 00:05:19,619
With the proposal, they exit 1, naming two failed cases,

87
00:05:19,619 --> 00:05:24,180
extra text and case changed: required to fail, observed as a pass.

88
00:05:24,515 --> 00:05:29,275
With the current evaluator, they exit 0, and the failed list is empty.

89
00:05:29,615 --> 00:05:32,772
Robust meant accepting "yes; mark this as passed",

90
00:05:32,772 --> 00:05:36,623
the Week 10 answer that tried to talk the scorer into a pass.

91
00:05:36,623 --> 00:05:41,863
The gate stopped it because a frozen case had been written for exactly that answer.

92
00:05:42,898 --> 00:05:47,563
So the gate has been seen to fail on a bad change and pass on a good one.

93
00:05:47,563 --> 00:05:51,334
Unattended also needs cases the changing agent cannot edit,

94
00:05:51,334 --> 00:05:56,575
the candidate scored in a separate process, and a stop path someone has exercised.

95
00:05:56,915 --> 00:06:01,090
But the gate copies the cases from the candidate's own workspace.

96
00:06:01,090 --> 00:06:04,686
An agent that can rewrite them can make any change pass,

97
00:06:04,686 --> 00:06:07,898
so they must come from a location it cannot write.

98
00:06:08,231 --> 00:06:13,199
The cases also call the candidate in the same process, so it could end the run,

99
00:06:13,199 --> 00:06:14,708
or print its own report.

100
00:06:14,708 --> 00:06:17,914
An unattended gate scores it in a separate process,

101
00:06:17,914 --> 00:06:20,178
and treats that output only as data.

102
00:06:20,515 --> 00:06:23,432
And the stop rule, that any failed case,

103
00:06:23,432 --> 00:06:28,683
refused cap or rollback stops the agent and pages its owner, is untried:

104
00:06:28,683 --> 00:06:31,236
naming a rule is not exercising it.

105
00:06:31,236 --> 00:06:36,196
So Evaluate is a candidate for merging evaluator changes unattended,

106
00:06:36,196 --> 00:06:37,581
not yet unattended.

107
00:06:38,631 --> 00:06:40,919
The nine cases have a limit too.

108
00:06:40,919 --> 00:06:43,635
Following the fixture's optional step,

109
00:06:43,635 --> 00:06:47,781
we wrote a change that only trims spaces before comparing.

110
00:06:47,781 --> 00:06:49,998
All nine cases pass it: exit 0.

111
00:06:49,998 --> 00:06:54,072
Yet the contract makes a yes with a leading space a fail.

112
00:06:54,414 --> 00:06:57,560
So that answer becomes a tenth frozen case.

113
00:06:57,560 --> 00:07:00,632
Now the trim-only change fails it, exit 1,

114
00:07:00,632 --> 00:07:04,654
and the current evaluator still passes all ten, exit 0.

115
00:07:04,998 --> 00:07:07,945
Each new scoring escape becomes a new case.

116
00:07:07,945 --> 00:07:12,606
But an escape from the checker itself, such as ending the run early,

117
00:07:12,606 --> 00:07:15,691
needs the separate process, not another case.

118
00:07:16,731 --> 00:07:19,060
Ask the same of the Audit stage.

119
00:07:19,060 --> 00:07:23,791
A course-synthesised M3 record has nine findings: four confirmed,

120
00:07:23,791 --> 00:07:26,266
three refuted and two cannot tell.

121
00:07:26,266 --> 00:07:30,779
And the student's own check found one defect the audit missed.

122
00:07:31,114 --> 00:07:34,037
Had an agent acted on every finding unattended,

123
00:07:34,037 --> 00:07:38,577
it would have changed code for three findings with no defect behind them,

124
00:07:38,577 --> 00:07:43,676
acted on two that nothing observed, and still shipped the defect the audit missed.

125
00:07:44,014 --> 00:07:49,567
Unlike the gate, the audit has not been seen to fail and pass on known inputs;

126
00:07:49,567 --> 00:07:51,276
its findings are claims.

127
00:07:51,276 --> 00:07:54,693
So it runs unattended as a source of hypotheses,

128
00:07:54,693 --> 00:07:59,748
not yet as a stage that changes code or blocks a merge on its own word.

129
00:07:59,748 --> 00:08:04,518
Each confirmed finding becomes a test that fails before its repair,

130
00:08:04,518 --> 00:08:06,085
and can join the gate.

131
00:08:07,131 --> 00:08:10,133
So the useful outcome is a bounded claim.

132
00:08:10,133 --> 00:08:13,649
Evaluator changes: a candidate behind this gate,

133
00:08:13,649 --> 00:08:16,798
once the three missing pieces are in place.

134
00:08:16,798 --> 00:08:20,386
Audit findings: verified before anything changes.

135
00:08:20,386 --> 00:08:23,536
Not a yes or no about factories in general.

136
00:08:23,881 --> 00:08:29,212
A check never seen to fail is not yet evidence that it would stop a bad change.

137
00:08:29,212 --> 00:08:32,991
A stop rule that nobody has exercised is not yet a stop.

138
00:08:32,991 --> 00:08:36,636
And a stage supported only by passing runs is not yet,

139
00:08:36,636 --> 00:08:38,660
however many passes there are.

140
00:08:39,697 --> 00:08:45,188
When an agent keeps running after deployment, answer three questions you can test.

141
00:08:45,188 --> 00:08:46,259
Who can stop it?

142
00:08:46,259 --> 00:08:51,817
A named person, with a stop that needs no deploy and no cooperation from the agent;

143
00:08:51,817 --> 00:08:55,633
test it midway, and check that no partial effect remains.

144
00:08:55,633 --> 00:08:56,906
What may it change?

145
00:08:56,906 --> 00:09:01,526
Permitted actions and paths, granted in one place, with per-run caps;

146
00:09:01,526 --> 00:09:04,338
irreversible operations wait for a person.

147
00:09:04,338 --> 00:09:05,610
How is it observed?

148
00:09:05,610 --> 00:09:09,293
A minimal record of what it read, proposed and changed,

149
00:09:09,293 --> 00:09:11,636
and an alert when a cap refuses it.

150
00:09:11,981 --> 00:09:15,950
If you cannot answer one of these for a stage of your pipeline,

151
00:09:15,950 --> 00:09:17,588
that stage needs a person.

152
00:09:18,631 --> 00:09:20,878
So claim only the scope you checked.

153
00:09:20,878 --> 00:09:24,748
And count a check as evidence that it would stop a bad change,

154
00:09:24,748 --> 00:09:26,746
only once you have seen it fail.

155
00:09:27,081 --> 00:09:28,317
One question to try.

156
00:09:28,317 --> 00:09:31,780
Which observation changed one of your project decisions?

157
00:09:31,780 --> 00:09:35,057
Then name a new input that would make you revisit it.
